boot.evidence: The Rust supervisor (forkpty + execv, PTY console drain, reap/restart policy) booted the real guest image through a Rust-written COW v3 header: markers RUSTDAEMON_GUEST_START, RUSTDAEMON_UNAME 'Linux (none) 7.2.0-rc4-opt #1 SMP ... aarch64', RUSTDAEMON_CPUCOUNT 4, RUSTDAEMON_WROTE, RUSTDAEMON_DONE, then the guest shut itself down and the daemon recorded phase=completed detail=exit=0.

rust_daemon_protocol_parity.evidence: ci/verify-daemon-parity.sh runs the C daemon and the Rust daemon in turn on the same runtime with the same client and diffs normalised replies: 6/6 lines identical (status, ports, exec, expose, state file, HTTP /status body). Exit code 3 when the socket is unreachable, as in C.

cow_isolation_rust_daemon.evidence: Controlled experiment around one Rust-daemon boot: backing image sha256 b363a716cd597efbe1022fc71113757f43e19aaa38a9fe76ac04bc6ed7e20d0a and mtime 2026-10-30 05:00:19 identical BEFORE and AFTER the boot; the guest booted (5 markers) and its COW file grew to 3222016512 bytes.

cow_writer_byte_exact.evidence: rust/src/cow.rs vs write_cow_header_file(): same 3 MiB image -> cmp identical, sha256 01b716b4d10f60c751ce0b65ef46039c94c05b79ef0e703d48b47895e4e0dee8 and same sparse size for both writers (CI gate). In a real boot both daemons produced byte-identical COW files: sha256 052c0be926c24af44c6a0418843a36c5253abb5e40900ff76b6a20963123f2f9.

rust_daemon_clean_shutdown.evidence: Guest powered off after completing its script; the Rust daemon logged phase=completed with detail=exit=0 and did not restart (exit 0 = finished session, restart only on crashes). 0 leftover linux-bionic processes after both the Rust and the C run.

rust_build_native_target.evidence: rustc host triple on Termux is aarch64-linux-android, so the device build IS the bionic target build: cargo test --release 30/30, clippy -D warnings clean, binary 1.6 MB (LTO + strip).

notes: The Rust port of the daemon boots a real UML guest, isolates writes with COW, shuts down cleanly and answers byte-identically to the C daemon on every control path checked. CAVEATS: (1) gvproxy lifecycle, exposure registry and the optional HTTP endpoint are ported and covered by the parity gate, but they were verified against a fake gvproxy socket and the C daemon's error paths -- not yet with a real gvproxy attached to a running guest. (2) An unrelated runit service (uml4termux, legacy shell flow 'uml4termux docker --foreground') was UP during this session and booted a persistent (non-COW) guest at 04:57-05:00, changing the backing image digest from 83f46631ef4df241a10e55b91612224c00d494ee1c608a294f6416a236a6a9ac to b363a716cd597efbe1022fc71113757f43e19aaa38a9fe76ac04bc6ed7e20d0a. That change is NOT attributable to the Rust daemon -- the controlled before/after experiment proves the Rust boot left the image byte-identical -- but any future image-digest claim must stop that service first. (3) The Rust daemon has not been exercised by a soak run or under the runit service; the C binary is still what ships in release v0.5.0.
known_limits_observed: gvproxy not attached during the boot test, so inbound exposure is unverified in the Rust daemon
